## 1. What this record covers, and what it does not
<!-- FIRST, not last. A pack that overstates its coverage is worse than no pack: the reader
     calibrates on the omissions, and finding one you did not disclose discredits the rest. -->
Covers: work performed through DevFlow skills in this repository over the range above.

Does **not** cover, and cannot:
- Agents run outside DevFlow skills — an editor completion, an ad-hoc CLI session, a teammate's local tooling. Nothing outside DevFlow is required to attribute itself, so an unattributed commit means "not produced by DevFlow", never "no agent involved".
- Third-party review bots (CodeRabbit, Bugbot and similar). Their record is the PR threads.
- Session telemetry — prompts, token counts, timings, which harness ran when. DevFlow keeps no such log; that is an OpenTelemetry-shaped problem and wants a separate system.
- Anything before {date DevFlow was adopted}, including the pre-DevFlow history of this repo.
- {any period where DECISIONS.md or trailers were absent — state it plainly if so}

## 5. Verification evidence
| Phase | Status | Truths | Smoke | Open human checks | Unverified |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| {03-orders} | {pass} | {7/7} | {pass} | {0} | {0} |

Evidence for every verified truth is an anchor — a command that ran, a test that passed, or a code path traced — recorded per phase in `VERIFICATION.md`. `unverified` counts truths the verifier **abstained** on as non-inferable rather than certifying; they are open questions, not defects.

## 6. Controls in force
- Fail-closed secret scan on every commit, every push, and every outbound bundle; a hit blocks and requires a human to clear it. Values are never echoed or logged — only file, line, and pattern class.
- Never commit to the base branch; all work lands on a feature branch and integrates by pull request.
- Human gates that agents may never self-answer: {list from autonomy.md}.
- `ARCHITECTURE.md` pins versions and carries a Forbidden list; deviations outside it stop as a decision checkpoint rather than an improvisation.
- `.env*` and key files are never opened; environment variables are referenced by name only.
